episode_title: Parents Worked SO HARD to Build the Business. Then, the DAUGHTER Took Over | Ginny Rosso

real_qa.q: What happened to KDI Designs staffing levels during and after COVID-19?
real_qa.r: KDI Designs had 18 people before COVID-19, but went down to 10 employees after the pandemic. Jenny noted that this reduction might have actually been a good thing in retrospect, as it led to a more streamlined operation.

real_qa.q: How did Jenny Rosso transition from resistant to becoming owner of KDI Designs?
real_qa.r: Jenny initially said during high school she would never become part of KDI Designs because of what she saw it do to her family. She went into event planning instead, realized hospitality required nights and weekends, and her father asked her to help out temporarily 14 years ago. The real shift came three years ago when her mother was diagnosed with ovarian cancer and had to step back, forcing Jenny into the leadership role.
real_qa.requete: Jenny Rosso KDI Designs took over mother cancer

real_qa.q: Why was Aldi kept secret during Jenny Rosso's childhood in a family business environment?
real_qa.r: Aldi was KDI Designs' largest client at the time and was an extremely private company, so Jenny's family had to protect its anonymity. Jenny and her brother learned they could not say 'Aldi' in public; instead they called it 'IDLA' (Aldi spelled backwards) when dining out. This taught them early how to act when supporting a business and protecting client confidentiality.
real_qa.requete: Aldi private company family business confidentiality

real_qa.q: What role did the Women Presidents Organization play in Jenny Rosso's battle with imposter syndrome?
real_qa.r: Jenny joined the Women Presidents Organization and walked into her first meeting feeling she did not deserve a seat at the table, thinking the other members were in companies 10 times larger and had done TED talks. Her husband told her she would not have been invited if she did not have the spark inside. A woman in the organization later told her that people with imposter syndrome are often the ones who deserve the seat most because they are humble and not cocky.
real_qa.requete: Women Presidents Organization imposter syndrome business owners

real_qa.q: How does KDI Designs measure success beyond revenue figures?
real_qa.r: Jenny emphasizes that success is not just about revenue but includes the ability to pick up her kids from school, achieve work-life balance, do eight-figure business, and have the flexibility to participate in activities like podcasts. She stresses that comparing gross profit to revenue is key, not raw revenue numbers, and that happiness, fulfillment, gratitude, and humility are equally important metrics of success.
real_qa.requete: business success beyond revenue gross profit balance

guest.bio_context: Jenny Rosso joined KDI Designs in 2012 after graduating from Northern Illinois University (NIU) with a hospitality degree. She worked her way up from receptionist through project coordinator, project manager, and account manager over 10 years before stepping into full leadership three years ago when her mother was diagnosed with ovarian cancer. She now solely operates KDI Designs, a commercial interior design firm in St. Charles, Illinois, which works with major clients including Aldi.

real_quote: I'm wildly successful because I can pick my kids up from school. I'm wildly successful because we are doing eight figures. I'm wildly successful because I can come sit with you and do a podcast.
